## Quick performance smoke preparation

Added a developer-only process-tree resource sampler for Linux and Windows, with optional psutil (not a runtime dependency). Records short CPU and summed RSS measurements for idle, navigation, several popouts and recovery; output stays local. Tested the sampling function against a synthetic Python parent/child in the execution container, not the Companion itself. RSS may double-count shared pages, short-lived processes can be missed; cold startup, relaunch and quit remain manual observations. No native measurements or performance claim yet. Existing regression and clean-install checks remain the verification path; no extra large QA phase.

## Local verification and settings regression correction

Owner log for 04950e94aea20aa92926399a3e915d9f050e5851: initial regression 396 passed, 52 skipped, 179 browser setup errors (missing Chromium); clean install PASS, all 629 locations and 33,405 encounter rows reachable, zero broken IDs. After installing Chromium, UI suite reported 166 passed, 20 skipped, 16 failed. All 16 failures reported `t is not a function`; localization matrix pinpointed Settings → Windows & popouts. Root cause: `toolPrefCard(t, def, caps)` shadowed the imported translator `t`. Renamed its tool ID parameter to `toolId`, preserving every setting key and popout action. Actual source evaluated with stubbed DOM helpers for 51 tool/language combinations, verifying translated Open button, correct popout target, setting key and slider keys. Added focused browser regression for all three languages; repeat failed matrices on owner machine. No full rendered pass or percentage claim yet. No version bump or distribution.

Tested application revision: `3388bb0d829d62a9b3e867100e7980c4ab8b1ec1`. Local localization suite: **64 passed**, exit 0 (152.52 s). Native capabilities reported pin, opacity, position, toasts and tray available. | Phase | Median summed RSS (MiB) | Peak summed RSS (MiB) | CPU (% of one logical core) |

All four samples were about five seconds; six processes, zero unreadable processes in each. CPU is modest on this system; summed RSS double-counts shared pages. Windows remains unverified. No new features, version bump or release.

## Balanced performance baseline and first implementation

Owner full regression at 3c8b634cc9afee24b82e53f5281736cce9a7611e: 581 passed, 52 skipped, zero failures, 677.09 s. Follow-up Linux PSS: 524.6 MiB baseline; 816.6/675.5 first open/close; 870.0/746.2 second open/close; processes 6/9/6/9/6 and none remaining after quit. Retention remains measurable, not a proven leak. Owner requires a lighter default before 0.8.0. First batch shares incremental Item Library rendering (main 240, popout 120) with cancellable observers; retains complete search/filter results. Pokédex releases grid observers and detached detail resize observers, limits card cache to current results, resets cached UI references on disposal and pauses grid animation when document hidden. Existing lazy still loading remains unchanged. 7 isolated actual-source batch assertions and JS syntax passed; new browser test added but not executed here. Further default optimization, actual native measurements and translated Performance controls remain pending. No promised RAM reduction until measured.

The older sprite regression explicitly required keeping the same DOM element across Home and excluded filters. That policy conflicts with the owner's new memory goal. Updated the regression deliberately: retain species API data (no refetch), reuse cards that remain in the current filtered results, release excluded cards and all detached cards on page exit, keep every generation and species accessible. Added browser observer lifecycle check. Both tests await execution; no claim of browser pass.

Selective popout redraw follow-up: ignore the main Pokédex last-opened species preference in floating grids, refresh saved filters in the grid, rely on the progress-run-keyed data cache instead of clearing species data on every display preference, debounce relevant redraws, and skip sprite-only updates to calculator, timers, natures and type chart. Footer controls update for their own opacity/text settings; mode/language still redraw completely. Fixed localized popout catalog count using existing key. 12 isolated decision checks and JS syntax passed. Browser lifecycle/regression and native before/after measurements pending.

Performance settings implementation: persisted Balanced (default), Lightweight, Full quality and Custom profiles. Item batches main/popout: 240/120 Balanced, 120/60 Lightweight, 480/240 Full quality; Custom selects batch and motion defaults independently. Lightweight defaults to static sprites; quality defaults to animated dex grid, other contexts unchanged. Explicit context/window preferences and global motion remain authoritative. No feature/alert/timer changes. Memory cleanup and lazy loading always active. Completed item batches release their cancellation closure; metadata settings events no longer reload settings across all windows. Added 24 EN/ES/zh catalog keys, route coverage and three-language browser regression; 28 isolated profile assertions and JS syntax passed. No fabricated cache-size or refresh controls. New code still awaits browser/native verification and measured improvement.

Balanced startup follow-up: defer 774,000+ bytes of bundled walkthrough and milestone translation source until needed in Spanish or Chinese. English and personally imported guides return original text without loading the large dictionaries. Storyline page, browse/search, Home continuation, floating storyline and shortcut feedback await the same existing hash-checked translation function at their asynchronous boundaries. No content removed. Five isolated reader cases and JS syntax passed; added browser request/translation regression, not yet run. Actual RAM benefit remains to measure.

Owner focused optimization run at 6bbad018fb89f09a135c3fea11bbf9581cb72af5: 104 passed, 12 skipped, one failed (317.48 s). The sole failure was the new grid observer test's initial assertion. Its Playwright add_init_script contained an uninvoked arrow function expression. Verified that evaluating the original source leaves the tracking Set undefined; evaluating the corrected IIFE installs the tracker and counts observe/unobserve calls in an isolated JS check. Reset saved filters/scope/language to a known test fixture and assert instrumentation separately. No application behavior changed; actual browser lifecycle check must still pass. Follow with comparative native PSS/CPU on Balanced, using the same original workflow.

Owner retest observer lifecycle: passed in 3.99 s at 2c236c5. Combined focused evidence: 105 passed, 12 skipped, zero unresolved failures (not a new single full suite). Balanced native follow-up PSS 537.2/744.0/635.1/867.5/723.5 MiB; CPU one-core percentages 24.9/2.4/26.6/51.7/24.3, process counts 6/9/6/9/6, no survivors at quit. Compared with original, first cycle better, second nearly unchanged and baseline slightly higher. Reused test profile, short sample windows; insufficient to establish repeatable savings or a leak. Found a concrete unnecessary Home refresh allocation: currentCard created a new sprite/ResizeObserver even when reusing an existing node. Pass the existing sprite into construction, and cancel pending countdown startup callbacks on disposal. Native settings pump now skips unrelated preferences instead of reapplying every popout's opacity/pin/lock etc. Preserve reset/restore handling. JS syntax checked; browser test and native validation pending. Next isolate animated Home vs static and minimal page CPU per process before changing default visuals or Qt architecture.

Owner automated native diagnostic at 6da264f: backend only 156.3 MiB PSS / 2.0% one core; simple tool 505.8 / 5.3%; Home 532.6 / 26.6%; attempted static Home 533.0 / 28.2%; normal again 533.0 / 26.3%; three popouts 677.8 then 689.8; after close 561.4 then 579.5. Main process grew 369.2 to 415.5 MiB while renderer returned to ~109 MiB and 1 process. The diagnostic loaded the same Home URL repeatedly, did not verify actual GIF absence, and may have reused the document; animation cost cannot be ruled out. Fresh profile differs from earlier measurements. Fixed startup work by making shell page modules and most popout-specific modules demand-loaded, with stale import navigation guard and prior module disposal on chrome rebuild. All modules remain bundled; no feature removal or engine change. Syntax checked, browser regression added, not yet run. Native engine fixed overhead remains substantial. Do not claim numerical savings for this commit until measured.

## Balanced optimization — lifecycle and demand-loading follow-up

- 4ea3157: Home render epoch invalidated on disposal; asynchronous builds stop before allocating abandoned cards, listeners or refresh timers. In-flight live refreshes are coalesced and late responses cannot restart disposed timers. Sprite references released on disposal. An isolated execution of actual Home source confirmed an outstanding request cannot register a timer/listener after disposal, even while its host still exists; browser regression added.
- 8ae053e: default onboarded Home does not load Pokédex or guide modules, or request run data, unless the relevant optional Home sections require them. Existing onboarding and optional cards remain supported. Added cold request-inventory regression.
- 131e907: guide timer/team editor modules load only when the storyline/custom-guide floating panels need them, not in unrelated popouts. Late Home action callbacks cannot overwrite another route. Extended calculator popout request-inventory regression.
- 60d48ab: optional developer sampler records complete proportional set size (PSS) when available, per-process end-of-sample figures, labelled revision/profile, and repeatable popout open/close cycles. Incomplete PSS is explicitly null, not an underestimated total. Added synthetic sampler tests.

JavaScript syntax and isolated Home cancellation check passed. New Python sampler tests, Playwright route/popout regressions and post-change native measurements have not been executed in this environment. Retain original 581-pass baseline and owner focused evidence separately. Do not claim a RAM/CPU improvement or change default visual quality until a comparable native test supports it. Main, release and version unchanged.
